content.comment_body: Hello everyone, for our OEE metric I want to record the date and time whenever a specific event takes place, such as when a counter changes. I'm planning to use VM mapping to extract these values.

The [product_name] only generates time stamps for events that are logged in its own Data Log if this feature is added in the program. Programmatically, [product_name] cannot access its system date and time to create a timestamp. You will need to implement timestamp generation manually within your OEE application. Alternatively, you can retrieve the date and time from [product_name] externally.

Thank you for your response. Could you specify which function block should be used to create the timestamp? From your explanation, it seems the timestamp logic needs to be developed within the OEE system.
I'm not sure what an OEE is. Regardless, [product_name] does not support timestamp creation through its own logic.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are looking for a way to automatically record the date and time (timestamp) whenever certain events occur, such as counter changes, using the [product_name] device. However, current product limitations prevent direct programmatic access to the system clock or automatic event-based timestamping. Users must design their own method for obtaining timestamps, typically by accessing the device's time externally or by adding customization outside the device's logic.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to provide simple, built-in functionality for retrieving system date and time in order to automate the creation of event-driven timestamps within the device's control logic.
pain_keywords: no programmatic access to date and time
